s1.syndrome_frame: Gastrointestinal syndrome with vomiting, hematemesis, and abdominal discomfort
salient_findings: Multiple rounded, echogenic neoformations at the pyloric antrum on abdominal ultrasound
Sessile, smooth-surfaced nodules in the pyloric antrum on endoscopy
key_facts: 9-month-old spayed female Ragdoll cat
Fed a raw rabbit-based raw food (BARF) diet for 3 months
Moderately dehydrated (≈7%)
Febrile (39.9°C)
Pale mucous membranes with capillary refill time ~3 s
Mild discomfort on abdominal palpation
Body condition score was 4/9 (4.2 kg)
Complete blood count, serum biochemistry, and FIV/FeLV tests were within normal limits or negative
Thoracic and abdominal radiographs were unremarkable
Abdominal ultrasound revealed multiple rounded, echogenic neoformations at the pyloric antrum
Mild mesenteric lymphadenomegaly
Cytological brushing of the gastric mucosa demonstrated mucosal cells, mixed neutrophilic and macrophagic inflammation, and occasional large, non-septate hyphae

shortlist.label: Phycomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Cytological brushing of the gastric mucosa demonstrated mucosal cells, mixed neutrophilic and macrophagic inflammation, and occasional large, non-septate hyphae

shortlist.label: Gastritis
shortlist.why_kept: Vomiting, hematemesis, and abdominal discomfort are consistent with gastritis, and cytological brushing showed mixed neutrophilic and macrophagic inflammation

shortlist.label: Gastric carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal ultrasound revealed multiple rounded, echogenic neoformations at the pyloric antrum, which could be consistent with a gastric tumor

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal foreign body
shortlist.why_kept: History of eating a raw rabbit-based diet could increase the risk of gastrointestinal foreign body

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic gastroenteritis
shortlist.why_kept: Cytological brushing showed mixed neutrophilic and macrophagic inflammation, and eosinophilic gastroenteritis could cause similar symptoms

raw.rationale: The presence of large, non-septate hyphae with irregular diameter and branching in the cytological brushing of the gastric mucosa, along with the clinical presentation of vomiting, hematemesis, and abdominal discomfort, supports the diagnosis of Phycomycosis, a fungal infection.

rejected.label: Gastritis
rejected.why: While gastritis could explain some symptoms, it does not account for the presence of fungal hyphae.

rejected.label: Gastric carcinoma
rejected.why: There is no mention of a mass or tumor in the provided information, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Gastrointestinal foreign body
rejected.why: The absence of any evidence of a foreign body on imaging and the presence of fungal elements make this diagnosis unlikely.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic gastroenteritis
rejected.why: This condition would likely show eosinophilic infiltration on cytology or histology, which is not mentioned in the provided information.
